provenance.note: A great temple bell struck by a wooden beam (bells-birds, his ask of 10-18: 'full root only for deep heavy bells with long low freq waves'). Its note is the hum, the lowest and longest of a cast bell's partials, so the row is struck two octaves under the call it plays (`oct` in the conversation row) and the strike the ear names is the prime an octave over the hum. The partials as a founder names them: the hum (1) and the prime (2) each a pair a hair apart, the minor-third tierce (2.38), the quint (3) and the nominal (4), each dying faster than the one under it. A beam's thud: a band at 300 Hz for 30 ms. The hum rings 34 s and the end is read off it.

notes.beating: The two pairs are the bell's 'wah': a great bell is never perfectly round, so each of its two lowest modes is two modes a fraction of a hertz apart, and they beat. At the hum's register (MIDI 40-55, 82-196 Hz) the hum's pair beats 0.17-0.41 Hz and the prime's 0.28-0.67 Hz, a slow swell and fall every two to six seconds. The spread is 0.17, so the pairs sum near the middle and the beat is a swell of the whole bell, as a bonshō's is, and not a motion from side to side.
notes.partials: Seven, under the conversation's ceiling of 32 oscillators: only the two pairs ring long (20-34 s), the tierce, the quint and the nominal are gone in 5-9 s, so a strike holds four oscillators once its colour has passed. The partials over the nominal are the beam's band.
notes.edge: Not read by the harmonic bus's edge, as vibes.
